newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Good Russian rye crop means few imports.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Good Russian rye crop means few imports.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
INCREASED RUSSIAN RYE OUTPUT TO CUT IMPORT REQUIREMENTS
MOSCOW, Feb 3 - Russia's rye output in 1996 rose to 5.9 million tonnes, 45 percent up on 1995's level.
The good result stems from an increase in the area sown to winter rye, which amounted to 4.15 million hectares, or 28 percent above the preceding year's level.
However, 1996 rye output remained well below the annual average seen over 1991-95.
Production increased everywhere in Russia, except for Siberia.
In Povolzhsk and the Central-Chernozem (Black Earth) region, output increased more than anywhere else in the country.
But despite a two-fold increase on 1995, rye output in even those areas did not reach the 1991-1995 average.
Still, Russia's rye imports, particularly from outside the Commonwealth of Independent States, are expected to be negligible in the first half of 1997.
